extracted.intended_audience: students, scholars, and creative writers studying literary theory and narrative technique
extracted.subtask_description: Analyze or produce literary texts using Russian Formalist concepts (e.g., literariness, defamiliarization, devices, fabula/syuzhet) to evaluate craft, narrative ordering, voice, and motif integration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literariness (Literaturnost)
rubrics_metrics.description: The properties that make a text literary rather than practical communication; the proper object of literary study is not biographical or sociological context but what makes language literary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the text for features that mark it as 'literary'—stylistic foregrounding, autonomous use of language, and devices that separate it from everyday practical communication. De-emphasize author biography or social context when focusing on literariness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defamiliarization (Ostranenie)
rubrics_metrics.description: Art makes the ordinary strange, restoring the freshness of perception that habit dulls. 'The technique of art is to make objects unfamiliar, to make forms difficult, to increase the difficulty and length of perception, because the process of perception is an aesthetic end in itself.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test of craft: does the work renew our perception of its subject? Look for techniques that render familiar things strange (unusual diction, unexpected perspective, deflected syntax). Consider whether the text increases the 'difficulty and length of perception' deliberately as an aesthetic aim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fabula vs. Syuzhet
rubrics_metrics.description: Fabula (story): the chronological raw events. Syuzhet (plot/discourse): the artistic ordering of those events as the reader encounters them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze how the syuzhet orders, delays, repeats, or omits elements of the fabula; assess the aesthetic effects produced by that ordering (tension, irony, surprise). Specifically evaluate 'how the artistic ordering distorts the chronological.'

rubrics_metrics.name: The Device (Priyom)
rubrics_metrics.description: Art is the sum of devices the artist manipulates — the device is the unit of literary craft.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventory and describe the devices used (examples given: repetition, parallelism, retardation, framing, displacement, inversion). Treat each device as a discrete operative unit and explain its contribution to overall effect, form, and meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Catalog of devices
rubrics_metrics.description: A text can be analyzed by its catalog of devices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produce a comprehensive listing of the work's devices and show how they function together. Use the catalog both descriptively (what devices are present) and evaluatively (which are dominant or subordinate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Motivation
rubrics_metrics.description: The justification for the inclusion of a device or motif within the narrative — realistic, compositional, or artistic motivation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each device or motif, ask whether its presence is motivated by realism (diegetic reasons), compositional necessity, or purely artistic aims. Use this to distinguish devices that serve plot/causal needs from those that are formal/artistic choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bound vs. Free Motifs
rubrics_metrics.description: Bound motifs: cannot be omitted without destroying the causal-temporal sequence. Free motifs: digressions, asides, tangents that contribute aesthetically but not causally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the proportion and integration of bound and free motifs. Evaluate how free motifs contribute aesthetically (texture, tone, theme) despite lacking causal necessity, and whether bound motifs structurally anchor the narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Dominant
rubrics_metrics.description: The structuring component of a work — the element that governs and transforms the others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the dominant element (formal device, theme, mode, or technique) and demonstrate how it organizes and reshapes other elements; use identification of the dominant to support claims about genre and style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skaz (oral/vernacular narrator)
rubrics_metrics.description: A first-person narrator with a strongly oral, vernacular voice — the narrator's manner of speaking is itself a device.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate narrator voice as an explicit device: assess orality, vernacular idiom, register, and how the skaz shapes perception, reliability, and aesthetic effect. Treat narrator manner as formally operative rather than merely representational.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetic function (Jakobson)
rubrics_metrics.description: Foregrounding of language's form (poetic function) as a criterion for analysis, associated with Roman Jakobson.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine passages for language that foregrounds itself (sound, rhythm, pattern) over referential content; assess how this poetic function contributes to literariness and to the work's dominant formal strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluative battery (synthesis of Formalist metrics)
rubrics_metrics.description: A text can be analyzed by: its catalog of devices; the relation of fabula to syuzhet; whether it defamiliarizes its subject; identifying the dominant element; the proportion and integration of bound/free motifs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating a work, synthesize the above criteria into a structured analysis: list devices, map fabula vs syuzhet, argue for presence/absence of ostranenie, nominate a dominant and justify it, and analyze motif types and integration. Use this composite approach rather than relying on a single metric.
